Subject: Melea, keeper of written accounts at the Theban palace. She is an adult woman in her early forties, a thoughtful custodian of copied testimony and household provisions. She has a medium olive complexion, a long oval face, brown eyes, fine freckles across her nose and dark brown hair gathered into a neat low braided bun. Her expression is attentive and quietly assured. She wears a simple ankle-length stone-colored woven linen dress, a plain muted blue-grey shawl over one shoulder, a narrow leather belt and practical leather sandals. Her clothes are carefully kept and lived in. One hand and forearm hold a small wooden wax writing tablet near her waist, with its dark wax face and a few shallow scratched rows visible as texture. Her free hand opens gently as she explains an account. The tablet is a small personal prop with a clear outline.

Subject: Melitta, the mountain keeper at Cithaeron and a speaker for her present worshipping group. She is an adult woman in her fifties with a sun-worn olive complexion, a broad angular face, strong brows, warm dark eyes and dark wavy hair streaked with grey and tied into one loose braid. Her expression is steady and welcoming, with the resolve of someone who knows the mountain paths and listens to her neighbors. She wears a simple ankle-length everyday wool robe in muted moss green, an earthy brown wool wrap, a plain woven belt and sturdy leather sandals. Show the natural wool weave, a few worn hems and practical layers suited to a wooded Greek slope. One hand holds a modest leafy ivy branch low at her side; her other hand opens clearly as she speaks. Her everyday robe and branch have a simple, grounded silhouette.
